extracted.intended_audience: parties, representatives, and practitioners involved in Michigan administrative hearings (MOAHR)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards from the Michigan Office of Administrative Hearings & Rules about how administrative hearings are conducted (including default remote hearings), contact/FOIA/media procedures, and which types of matters MOAHR handles. Useful for parties preparing for or requesting modifications to hearing format or seeking agency contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default remote hearings policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to MOAHR Administrative Hearing Standard 2024-1, administrative proceedings will by default be conducted remotely, unless: (i) an administrative law judge or hearing officer determines in their discretion that all or part of a proceeding should be in person or (ii) a party submits a written request demonstrating good cause for why all or part of the proceeding should be in person and the administrative law judge or hearing officer finds the request should be granted because of accessibility limitations, specific evidentiary issues, or other unique circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference Administrative Hearing Standard 2024-1 for the default remote-first rule and the allowable exceptions (judge discretion or granted written requests showing good cause such as accessibility limitations, evidentiary issues, or other unique circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and Guidelines for Remote Hearings (scope and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: MOAHR has developed a Standards and Guidelines for Remote Hearings manual that contains useful information and best practices relevant to the conduct of remote hearings for all practice areas within MOAHR, except for the Corrections area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the manual for practical best practices when participating in remote hearings; note that Corrections-area hearings are excluded from this manual's coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency jurisdiction/exception for driver's license restoration hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: MOAHR does not conduct driver’s license restoration hearings, which are handled by the Michigan Department of State’s Office of Hearings and Administrative Oversight (OHAO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions regarding a driver’s license restoration hearing, contact MDOS Call Center: 888-767-6424, Email: SOS-AHS@michigan.gov, or use the MDOS website (michigan.gov/sos → View All Services → Request a Hearing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Rules Division responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Rules Division is charged with overseeing the administrative rulemaking process for each department in the State of Michigan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders seeking information about rulemaking oversight should consult the Administrative Rules Division resources linked on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting MOAHR (main office and local hearing site details)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the main office please call 517-335-2484 or email MOAHR-GA@michigan.gov. There is also often a local hearing site phone and fax number listed on the Notice of Hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the main office contact for general inquiries; always check the Notice of Hearing for site-specific contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on how to submit a FOIA request is provided via the LARA FOIA Request process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the LARA FOIA request instructions (linked on the MOAHR page) to submit public records requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media attendance policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Media who wish to attend a hearing must follow the MOAHR Media Policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the MOAHR Media Policy linked on the site for procedures and any requirements for media attendance at hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who will hear my appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An Administrative Law Judge from MOAHR will hear your appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should prepare for proceedings before an MOAHR Administrative Law Judge and use available MOAHR resources to understand procedures and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of hearings conducted by MOAHR
rubrics_metrics.description: MOAHR conducts a range of hearings including Employment Hearings, Unemployment Appeal Hearings, Michigan Employment Relations Commission matters, Benefit Services Hearings, Licensing Hearings (e.g., Liquor Control Commission Licensing, Health Care Professional Licensing), Regulatory Hearings (e.g., MIOSHA, Wage & Hour), and Corrections Hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the site’s sections (Employment, Benefits, Licensing, Regulatory, Corrections) for area-specific FAQs, procedures, and links to case decisions or resources.
